(1) the Warburg impedance is not necessarily due to a diffusion process; (2) Warburg impedance can be induced by grain boundaries; (3) the impedance of a polycrystal with grain boundaries is described by a circuit that consists of three elements: a resistor (R), a capacitor (C) and a Warburg impedance (W).

(1) Warburg-type impedance is induced by grain boundaries in polycrystals, not only by the electrodes, and (2) the impedance of a mixed conductor with a semi-blocking boundary is a superposition of impedances of two mixed conductors with different boundary conditions.

the analysis of impedance spectra of mixed conductors should be based on generalised circuit models that take into account all the relevant processes in the system, and not on simplified models that are based on a-priori assumptions.
